scope: Dioxus 0.7 documentation, including the optional Fullstack and Router packages.

ssr.note: Dioxus Fullstack renders initial HTML and hydrates the application in the browser.
ssr.label: Fullstack

streaming.note: Fullstack can opt into out-of-order HTML streaming. The default waits for suspense boundaries before sending the page.
streaming.label: Fullstack

suspense.note: Suspense boundaries coordinate asynchronous UI; Fullstack can stream their resolved HTML.

client.note: Fullstack supports hydration of the server-rendered application.
client.label: Hydration

ssg.note: Fullstack SSG runs the app, enumerates its sitemap, and retains HTML for static hosting.
ssg.label: Fullstack SSG

csr.note: The web target renders and updates UI in the browser through the WASM runtime.

serverOnly.note: Server-only blocks and server functions stay on the server; normal Fullstack components also execute during browser hydration.
serverOnly.label: Server blocks / functions

partialRendering.note: The reviewed static/incremental renderer does not establish a prebuilt shell with per-request dynamic UI holes.

routing.note: The fullstack server integrates an Axum router and registers server functions.
routing.label: Fullstack / Axum

layouts.note: The official Router nests routes inside layout components with Outlet.
layouts.label: Dioxus Router

dynamicRoutes.note: Routable derives typed dynamic, catch-all, query, and hash route segments.
dynamicRoutes.label: Dioxus Router

parallelRoutes.note: Nested Outlet layouts are documented, but not independently navigable named route slots.

interceptedRoutes.note: The reviewed navigation guide does not define intercepted-modal and direct-link rendering semantics.

prefetch.note: Link and Navigator navigation are documented; automatic route/data prefetch is not established by the reviewed guide.

softNavigation.note: dioxus-router Link/Navigator update internal routed UI and history without fetching a new document. External navigation can leave the application; the router also serves non-browser targets.
softNavigation.label: dioxus-router

viewTransitions.note: The reviewed routing API does not establish this navigation capability. Application code or another package may provide it; this finding is not proof of absence.

redirects.note: Navigator and router callbacks can replace/redirect navigation; server responses can separately set HTTP redirects.
redirects.label: Dioxus Router

serverData.note: use_loader resolves data during SSR and serializes its result for the initial client render.
serverData.label: Fullstack use_loader

clientData.note: Reactive resources expose pending/result state and can restart when dependencies change. This is not a shared query cache.
clientData.label: Resources

requestDedupe.note: The resource lifecycle guide does not establish a request-wide keyed cache shared across separate components.

persistentCache.note: The incremental renderer retains generated HTML in its configured static directory. This is an HTML cache, not an application data cache.
persistentCache.label: Fullstack incremental renderer

invalidation.note: Reactive resources expose restart to re-run their asynchronous work, and reactive dependencies can trigger refresh. This is resource-level invalidation; it does not establish automatic tag/path purging of retained HTML or a shared server cache.
invalidation.label: Resource restart / dependency refresh

isr.note: Incremental rendering can retain generated pages; freshness, regeneration triggers, and deployment behavior require renderer configuration.
isr.label: Incremental HTML renderer

apiRoutes.note: Fullstack’s Axum router can register custom HTTP handlers alongside generated server functions.
apiRoutes.label: Fullstack / Axum

httpErrors.note: Fullstack maps errors bubbling to the root into HTTP statuses, with unknown errors defaulting to 500. A custom ErrorBoundary must explicitly call FullstackContext::commit_error_status to preserve the intended error status when it catches an error. Rendering a fallback alone does not set that status; response decisions must precede committed headers.
httpErrors.label: Fullstack error statuses

actions.note: Fullstack registers server functions that browser code can call.
actions.label: Fullstack

forms.note: Form<T> deserializes typed form inputs; MultipartFormData handles uploads. Business validation remains application code.
forms.label: Fullstack forms

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Form<T> deserializes typed form inputs; MultipartFormData handles uploads. Business validation remains application code.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Tower/Axum middleware and per-server-function middleware are supported.
middleware.label: Fullstack / Axum

cookies.note: Axum extractors and response headers provide request cookie integration; session policy requires application code.
cookies.label: Axum integration

cssModules.note: The reviewed CSS/SCSS and stylesheet guide does not document CSS Modules class-name compilation.

scopedCss.note: Stylesheets and inline styles are documented; automatic component-local selector rewriting is not established.

tailwind.note: Dioxus 0.7 integrates automatic Tailwind processing in its CLI workflow. Tailwind remains the external CSS compiler, but Dioxus supplies the build integration rather than requiring only an application-authored standalone recipe.
tailwind.label: Integrated Tailwind workflow

cssInJs.note: Inline styles do not establish a CSS-in-JS compiler or SSR style registry in the reviewed guide.

images.note: Manganis asset processing supports build-time image resizing and format conversion.
images.label: Manganis

fonts.note: Font files can be bundled as assets; automatic font subsetting and fallback-metric optimization are not established.
fonts.label: Bundled font files

scripts.note: document::eval and browser bindings execute app-authored JavaScript. This is not an optimized third-party script scheduling API.
scripts.label: Document eval

assetPipeline.note: The Dioxus CLI processes assets declared with asset!, hashes their output names, and resolves Asset handles to the built URLs. This includes images and other files; hashing can be explicitly disabled. Arbitrary literal URLs do not gain this behavior.
assetPipeline.label: Manganis / asset!

staticAssets.note: asset! bundles and fingerprints files through Manganis.
staticAssets.label: Manganis

metadata.note: Document head components expose titles/meta/links. SEO-critical head content must resolve in the initial stream chunk.
metadata.label: Document components

dynamicMetadata.note: Head components accept reactive values; metadata rendered after the first chunk may only appear after client hydration.
dynamicMetadata.label: Initial-chunk constraint

metadataInheritance.note: The reviewed head component guide does not define metadata-object inheritance through nested route layouts.

metadataOverrides.note: The reviewed document API does not establish a standard nested metadata-field merge/clear contract.

titleTemplates.note: Title components are documented, but an ancestor title-formatting/absolute-title API is not established.

socialImages.note: Image asset transforms are documented; a route-aware generated social-card renderer is not established.

sitemaps.note: The SSG workflow enumerates app routes through a sitemap for prerendering. This is not evidence of a crawler XML sitemap generator.
sitemaps.label: SSG route enumeration

robots.note: The CLI’s public asset directory can publish an application-authored robots.txt at its unchanged public path. The file’s directive contents and deployment policy are application-owned; this is not a typed crawler-directive generator.
robots.label: Public asset file

markdown.note: The reviewed asset guide does not establish a Markdown page/compiler integration; add a parser/content package.

collections.note: Asset bundling does not establish typed content collection schemas, loaders, and queries.

draftMode.note: Application middleware can authorize previews; a dedicated draft-preview/cache-bypass API is not established.

translations.note: dioxus-i18n provides Fluent messages and locale configuration; its documentation declares Dioxus 0.7 support.
translations.label: dioxus-i18n

localeRouting.note: The typed dynamic-route guide demonstrates a locale segment; negotiation and language redirects are application policy.
localeRouting.label: Typed locale segment

localeFormatting.note: The guide introduces dioxus-i18n messages but does not establish a number/date formatter API for this comparison.

auth.note: The guide explicitly leaves authentication to libraries/application code and demonstrates axum_session_auth.
auth.label: axum_session_auth

csp.note: Application middleware can supply headers; automatic CSP nonce/hash coordination is not established by the reviewed Fullstack guide.

cspNonce.note: The reviewed security/rendering API does not establish coordinated per-response CSP nonces for generated scripts and styles. Hash-based CSP and application-authored headers are different mechanisms.

csrf.note: Typed form parsing does not establish CSRF tokens or origin enforcement; the reviewed forms guide does not document that protection.

environment.note: Server-function bodies and extractors stay on the server. Application code must keep secrets out of serialized results and client modules.
environment.label: Server-function boundary

types.note: Rust checks component/route types; Routable derives typed route parameters.

hmr.note: RSX and CSS support hot reload; some Rust changes rebuild, and Rust hotpatching is experimental.

cli.note: The dx toolchain configures, serves, and bundles Dioxus applications.
cli.label: Dioxus CLI

bundleAnalysis.note: The reviewed bundling configuration does not establish an interactive production module-size analyzer.

unitTests.note: The guide uses Rust tests and dioxus_ssr snapshots; hook testing requires manually driving a VirtualDom.
unitTests.label: Rust / SSR test recipe

e2eTests.note: The official browser-testing guide configures Playwright against a served web app.
e2eTests.label: Playwright

observability.note: The first-party logger connects tracing to native or web logging destinations. Metrics/tracing backends require additional configuration.
observability.label: Dioxus logger

errorHandling.note: ErrorBoundary captures component errors and renders fallback UI.

serverHosting.note: The production Fullstack integration runs an Axum application server.
serverHosting.label: Fullstack / Axum

subpathProxy.note: The CLI documents web.app.base_path for subdirectory builds. Its web.proxy setting is a development API proxy, not production reverse-proxy support. Production Fullstack routing, server-function URLs, browser routing and forwarded origin must also agree with the deployment; the CLI setting alone does not establish that complete contract.
subpathProxy.label: Build base; host setup

staticHosting.note: SSG emits retained HTML for static hosting; dynamic server functions still require a server.
staticHosting.label: Fullstack SSG

containers.note: The reviewed bundle/configuration guide does not document a web-server container image workflow.

edgeHosting.note: The reviewed Fullstack host is Axum; a worker/edge runtime adapter is not established.

orm.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned orm / query builder API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

migrations.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned schema migrations API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

transactions.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned transactions API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

jobs.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned background jobs API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

mail.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned email API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

uploads.note: Fullstack server functions accept FileStream upload arguments. A durable file/storage lifecycle is not supplied by this transport alone.
uploads.label: FileStream transport

realtime.note: Dioxus 0.7 Fullstack server functions support typed WebSockets with a use_websocket client hook. This supplies a real-time transport; applications still own authorization, message semantics and distributed pub/sub.
realtime.label: Fullstack typed WebSockets

xssEscaping.note: RSX text interpolation renders text; dangerous_inner_html is the explicit raw-HTML bypass. Treat its input as trusted or sanitize it outside the renderer.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific rate limiting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: The linked server API review does not establish the specific progressive forms contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

optimisticUi.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific optimistic updates contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

requestCancellation.note: use_resource reruns reactive asynchronous work and exposes cancellation/restart. Fetch cancellation depends on the future/transport; canceling UI work does not roll back a remote mutation.
requestCancellation.label: use_resource

typedLinks.note: The Routable derive generates typed route variants and parameters used by Link/navigation. A string URL can bypass that typed route API; Router is an optional package.
typedLinks.label: dioxus-router / Routable

searchParams.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific validated url state contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

codeSplitting.note: Dioxus 0.7’s WASM-Split/CLI integration supports split WebAssembly bundles and lazy loading. Use the documented splitting workflow; this is not a claim that every Rust dependency or all routes split automatically.
codeSplitting.label: Dioxus CLI / WASM-Split
